source_name: AJPES / company-data aggregators (companywall.si, bizi.si) for Bankart and peers
why_relevant: Company registry mirrors carrying filed financials, ownership, directors and activity codes for Bankart, KDD and related operators — the objective corporate-fact layer beneath self-published marketing, and the way to detect ownership shifts among the five owner banks.

source_name: Racunalniske novice — Bankart partner profile (SI IT trade media)
why_relevant: Slovenian IT trade outlet carrying a paid/partner profile of Bankart. Local trade media of this kind routinely publish vendor-partner directories and sponsored interviews that surface SI payments vendors invisible to English-language search.

source_name: Banka Slovenije – Register družb za izdajo elektronskega denarja (EMI register)
why_relevant: Authoritative national register of licensed e-money institutions, their agents and branches; the definitive list of licensed non-bank competitors (e.g. Paywiser) and of entries/deletions signalling market entry and exit.

source_name: Banka Slovenije – Plačilne institucije držav EGP v Sloveniji (EEA passporting-in list)
why_relevant: Lists cross-border PSPs/EMIs passported into Slovenia — the main channel by which foreign acquirers, wallets and PSPs (SumUp, Revolut-type players) legally compete for Slovenian merchants without a local licence.

source_name: Banka Slovenije – Register subjektov nadzora entry: Paywiser d.o.o.
why_relevant: Entity-level regulatory record for the leading Slovenian hybrid EMI; gives licence number/date and permitted services — the ground truth against which Paywiser's commercial claims can be checked.

source_name: Paywiser – corporate site (SL/EN)
why_relevant: Primary vendor source for Slovenia's flagship licensed EMI/PSP: product pages, card issuing, IBAN/wallet offer, terms & conditions and regional pages reveal target segments and partner banks.

source_name: mBills – mobile wallet site (merchant section)
why_relevant: Merchant-facing pages of the main bank-independent Slovenian mobile wallet: acceptance model (barcode at POS), merchant onboarding, FAQ and company background; direct competitor to bank wallets and to Flik at the point of sale.

source_name: FURS (Financial Administration) news – 'Prenehanje delovanja mBills'
why_relevant: State-agency notice about mBills ceasing to be an eDavki payment option, listing which wallets remain accepted (Flik, VALÚ) — an authoritative, non-marketing indicator of wallet viability and of which rails the public sector supports.

source_name: VALÚ – Telekom Slovenije smart wallet site
why_relevant: Telco-owned wallet competing for P2P, P2M and e-commerce payments; site documents merchant acceptance network, VALÚ Moneta carrier-billing legacy and consumer proposition.

source_name: Telekom Slovenije – sporočila za medije (press releases)
why_relevant: Issuer of VALÚ announcements: launch, ecosystem strategy, user/transaction growth numbers and merchant partnerships (Petrol, MOL, OMV, Mercator, Tuš, Pošta Slovenije, McDonald's) — rare quantified competitor metrics.

source_name: Bankart – FLIK e-commerce / processor site
why_relevant: Bankart is the national card/instant-payment processor and the operator behind Flik; its e-commerce pages document how the bank-owned scheme is being pushed into merchant checkout, the key defensive rail against non-bank wallets.

source_name: Eligma / GoCrypto – crypto acceptance network
why_relevant: Slovenian company operating the GoCrypto merchant crypto-acceptance network (settlement to merchants in EUR, integrations with Binance Pay and wallets); the clearest non-bank, non-card acceptance competitor that mainstream banking press underreports.

source_name: gov.si – seznam registriranih ponudnikov storitev virtualnih valut (VASP/CASP register)
why_relevant: State portal hosting the register of registered virtual-currency service providers — the licensing counterpart to crypto payment players; needed to enumerate crypto competitors under MiCA/AML supervision.

source_name: Nexi Group – corporate press releases & merchant/acquiring pages
why_relevant: Nexi is the dominant regional acquirer/processor with a Slovenian entity; group press releases carry partnership news (e.g. PayPal collecting-PSP arrangement, bank partnerships) that lands in the Slovenian market without local announcements.

source_name: thebanks.eu – EMI list for Slovenia
why_relevant: English-language aggregator that enumerates Slovenian EMIs with profile pages; useful cross-check and entity-discovery shortcut against the BSI registers, but secondary — always confirm against BSI.

source_name: Revolut – Slovenian legal/terms and Revolut Pay merchant pages
why_relevant: Localised legal and fee documents show exactly which services a large cross-border EMI offers Slovenian consumers and merchants (Revolut Pay checkout), and price points that pressure bank acquiring.

source_name: SumUp – Slovenian support/merchant centre
why_relevant: mPOS provider targeting Slovenian micro-merchants with no monthly fee; localised help centre documents accepted methods, hardware and payout mechanics — the low end of the acquiring market banks are losing.

source_name: Računalniške novice – tech/business news (payments market entries)
why_relevant: Slovenian tech trade outlet that covers vendor market entries and product launches (e.g. the leading European mPOS provider entering Slovenia) earlier and in more detail than general business press.

source_name: Monitor.si – IT magazine (fintech/wallet partnership coverage)
why_relevant: Reported the Petrol–mBills strategic tie-up; Monitor consistently covers wallet/merchant partnerships that never appear in English sources.

source_name: Forbes Slovenija (forbes.n1info.si) – payments business coverage
why_relevant: Carries quantified market data on Slovenian payment rails (reported Flik user and transaction volumes, share of online payments) and profiles of local payment startups — rare source of usable numbers.

source_name: Delo.si – payments and banking reporting
why_relevant: National daily covering the bank-side response to fintech competition (instant-payment app rollout, regulatory clearance for Flik); useful for chronology and for named institutional actors.

source_name: Startup.si – Slovenian startup portal (fintech/open banking)
why_relevant: Government-adjacent startup portal that surfaces early-stage Slovenian payment/open-banking ventures (e.g. Fliqa and its cooperation intent with Bankart) long before they appear in banking press — a snowball source for new actor names.

source_name: fintech.svetidej.com – Slovenian fintech services directory
why_relevant: Directory-style catalogue of fintech services available in Slovenia; a cheap enumeration layer for consumer-facing non-bank providers to feed the actor map.

source_name: Slo-Tech forum – payments threads (VALÚ vs mBills etc.)
why_relevant: Largest Slovenian tech community; threads reveal real merchant acceptance friction, fee complaints and product changes for wallets before/without official communication — an indirect signal source, not evidence.

source_name: European Commission DG COMP merger case files (M.10075 Nexi/Nets)
why_relevant: Merger decisions contain detailed, evidence-based descriptions of acquiring/processing market structure and national shares, including CEE markets — one of the few sources with structural competitive data on acquirers.

source_name: NLB Group – Press Releases (EN mirror)
why_relevant: English mirror of the SL newsroom; useful for cross-checking dates and for items published only in EN (investor/regulatory). Confirms which announcements NLB considers group-level vs Slovenia-only.

source_name: NLB Skupina – Strategija 2030 (strategy / digital transformation page)
why_relevant: States NLB's digital-transformation priorities (omnichannel platform, data/AI). Signals what vendor categories the bank will buy next — a forward indicator complementing the backward-looking press releases.
